## Reading the graph first

Two different numbers matter here and the scan reports both:

- **fan-in** = direct importers → how much *ripple* an edit causes.
- **fan-out** = direct imports → how much *context* the file drags in, and how easy it is to change safely.

`blast_radius_importers` is the transitive closure, and it re-orders things: `src/log.ts` has only 9 direct importers but **30** transitive ones — the widest reach in the repo — while `src/index.ts` has fan-out 17 but only **7** transitive importers.

The triage rule that falls out: **refactor the high-fan-out, low-fan-in orchestrators first** (all the size, none of the ripple), **stabilise the high-fan-in hubs second**, and **leave the leaf utilities alone** no matter how ugly their findings look.

---

## Tier 1 — refactor first (max size reduction, minimum ripple)

**1. `src/index.ts`** — fan-out **17** (p99 cutoff is 11), fan-in **4**, 7 transitive importers · `crime_00070`, `crime_00068`
The worst offender by volume and the cheapest to fix. 460 lines hosting `build` at 293 lines (4.9× threshold, `crime_00023`), an anonymous 274-line arrow (`crime_00024`), `mainTasks` at 194 (`crime_00025`), plus `normalizeOptions` (96), `startWatcher` (79), `buildAll` (75). Fan-out 17 with fan-in 4 is the signature of an orchestrator: it *pulls* the whole codebase together but almost nothing depends on its internals. Extract helpers here and only 7 files can possibly notice. It also carries `test_gap: 0` — there is a test suite behind it.

**2. `src/esbuild/index.ts`** — fan-out **11** (exactly p99), fan-in **1**, `test_gap: 0` · `crime_00069`
`runEsbuild` is 237 lines (4.0×, `crime_00022`) and reads **38 distinct properties** off one untyped `options` bag (`crime_00040`). Fan-in of 1 means restructuring is effectively free — a single caller to update. The 38-property option bag is the real agent hazard: an agent editing this function cannot see which fields are load-bearing.

**3. `src/cli-main.ts`** — not in the connectivity tier at all, 2 transitive importers · `crime_00006`
`main` is 153 lines (2.5×) with high severity and confidence 0.95, and the file is a graph leaf. This is a pure-win refactor: nothing downstream can break. Do it whenever you have a spare hour; it needs no coordination.

---

## Tier 2 — high value, but load-bearing (do second, mechanically)

**4. `src/utils.ts`** — fan-in **18**, 29 transitive importers, 425 lines · `crime_00039`, `crime_00044`
Fan-in 18 is 2× the p95 cutoff (9) and well past p99 (10) — this is the highest-coupling node in the repo, and it's also a God File with 7 sync I/O calls in `removeFiles` / `ensureTempDeclarationDir` (`crime_00010`). Splitting it genuinely reduces blast radius, which is why it's not in the "leave alone" pile. But it touches 18 importers, so do it as a **move-and-re-export** (split into modules, keep `utils.ts` as a barrel), not a rewrite — and only after Tier 1, so you aren't holding two large refactors open at once.

**5. `src/plugin.ts`** — fan-in **10** (at the p99 line), fan-out 3, 29 transitive importers, `test_gap: 0.75` · `crime_00008`, `crime_00002`
`buildFinished` is 103 lines and highest agent-risk in the whole report (0.54). The blocker is the combination: **10 importers and no test coverage**. That's the one place in this repo where a refactor is genuinely unsafe. Add tests around `buildFinished` first, then extract. Prefer additive changes until then.

---

## Leave alone

**`src/log.ts`** — fan-in 9, **fan-out 0**, 30 transitive importers · `crime_00021`
The widest transitive reach in the repo, and precisely why you don't touch it. Fan-out 0 means it depends on nothing, so it cannot break from below; 30 downstream files mean any restructuring is pure churn. Its only findings are two unprefixed booleans (`onlyImportant`, `silent` — `crime_00019`). The detector says "split or invert"; here that advice is wrong — this is a healthy stable leaf, not coupling debt. At most, rename the booleans in place.

**`src/rollup.ts`** — **fan-in 0**, fan-out 7, **0** transitive importers · `crime_00048`
Nothing imports it. Refactoring it reduces blast radius across the codebase by exactly zero, so it doesn't belong in a blast-radius plan — despite having a 122-line `getRollupConfig` (`crime_00015`) and a real `False Identity` problem (a `get*` name that calls `setSilent` and `removeFiles`, `crime_00009`). Fix the misleading name opportunistically when you're next in the file; that's a 5-minute correctness-of-naming fix, not a triage priority.

**`src/api-extractor.ts`** — fan-in 1, fan-out **6** (exactly the p95 cutoff) · `crime_00043`
Sits right on the threshold, so it's borderline by construction. One importer. Nothing to gain.

**`test/utils.ts`** — fan-in 9 · `crime_00087`
Test infrastructure. Fan-in 9 is real, but the blast radius is confined to the test suite.

**`docs/README.md`** — 679 lines, **`severity: high`** · `crime_00051`
The highest-severity `large_file` in the report and the clearest trap: it's markdown, with `blast_radius_importers: 0`. No code depends on it. Severity ≠ priority — rank on aggregate risk, and its `agent_risk` is 0.27. (Splitting it would help the separate `missing_agent_context` problem, `crime_00011`, but that's a docs task with its own justification.)

**`src/esbuild/postcss.ts` / `svelte.ts`** — big functions (140, 126, 116 lines) but not in the connectivity tier and 7 transitive importers each. Plugin leaves. Queue behind Tier 2.

---

## Two caveats on this ranking

**`churn: 0` on every single finding.** There is no git-history signal in this scan, so the entire ordering is static coupling. If real churn data exists, a moderately-coupled file that changes weekly should outrank a heavily-coupled file nobody has touched in a year — re-run and re-rank if you have history.

**The `test_gap: 0` on Tier 1 is softer than it looks.** I leaned on it to justify refactoring `src/index.ts` first, but the scan also flags `test/index.test.ts` with a test containing **0 assertions** (`crime_00060`) and seven more using only weak matchers (`crime_00077`–`crime_00083`). Coverage exists; some of it doesn't assert anything. Before the `build`/`mainTasks` extraction, harden the assertions in `test/index.test.ts` — otherwise the safety net you're relying on is partly decorative.
